newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mexico's Ortiz says GDP growth may be above 4.0 pc.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says GDP growth may be above 4.0 pc.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz on Friday stuck to an official 1997 forecast of 4.0 percent GDP growth but added he would not argue with private sector analysts' higher predictions.

"We're not revising official forecasts, but most private sector analysts predict that the economy will be growing at between 4.5 and 5.0 percent," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

Mexico was plunged into recession in 1995 after a sudden peso devaluation. Since then it has engineered an export-led recovery and earlier this month Ortiz said preliminary figures showed 1996 GDP had risen about 4.6 percent.

Some investors however are concerned that imports are on the rise and fear this may erode Mexico's recovery. Exports outpaced imports by only $220 million in December, preliminary official data showed last week.
But Ortiz said growth in imports was not surprising.

"It's something to be expected since the economy is growing strongly," he said. "It's good that imports are growing, particularly imports of capital goods, because that shows that the investment process is coming along."
He said local and foreign investment in Mexico looked like the engine for the next phase of growth.

"What we are seeing is a strong investment process on the part of domestic and foreign investors and I think this is going to be the largest single contribution to growth in 1997," he said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 2734
